articles.title: Home Assistant restores UniFi controller certificate checks
articles.dek: The Verify SSL setting checks the controller’s identity, so invalid certificates can require attention.
body: Home Assistant restores certificate checks for UniFi Network connections with Verify SSL enabled. A conflicting connection setting had silently disabled those checks for both ordinary requests and live updates. Eric Constantin makes his first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the correction.

Controllers using an untrusted, expired or mismatched certificate can therefore stop connecting when this correction is adopted. Keeping verification enabled requires a certificate chain trusted by Home Assistant and a configured hostname matching the certificate. Connections with verification deliberately disabled retain their existing behaviour.

pullRequests.title: Fix SSL certificate verification in UniFi Network

articles.title: Home Assistant updates Shelly devices too old to finish setup
articles.dek: A repair opens the firmware updater before the device’s other controls can load.
body: Home Assistant gives Shelly devices running unsupported firmware a way to update without first completing ordinary setup. Instead of stopping at a setup failure, the connection exposes only its firmware updater and raises a repair that starts the update.

When the device reports supported firmware, Home Assistant reloads the connection and adds its normal controls and readings. The contributor tested the path with a Shelly 1PM running firmware from 2019 and a Shelly Plus Plug S running a pre-1.0 beta.

pullRequests.title: Allow firmware update of Shelly devices running unsupported firmware

articles.title: ESPHome turns music controllers into automation inputs
articles.dek: Musical keyboards, pads and foot switches using Bluetooth MIDI can trigger maker-defined automations.
body: ESPHome adds a Bluetooth MIDI connection for makers who want to use a musical keyboard, pad controller or foot switch as an input. Notes, knob movements and other MIDI messages can trigger automations, and the device can send MIDI messages back.

Bogdan Rădulescu brings the generic connection from his external component, which he reports using for four months with an M-Vave SMC-PAD and a Korg microKEY Air. Assigning particular buttons or notes to lights and other actions remains up to the maker; the component does not create those controls automatically.
This is Rădulescu’s first contribution to ESPHome.

pullRequests.title: [ble_midi] Add BLE MIDI component

articles.title: Home Assistant gives Powerwall charging a time and power limit
articles.dek: Local dispatch returns the battery to normal operation automatically when its timer ends.
body: Home Assistant’s Teslemetry connection adds an action to charge or discharge a paired Powerwall at a specified power for a specified duration. The command travels through the local gateway, and the battery returns to its normal operation when the time expires.

A second action ends the dispatch early and resumes normal operation immediately. This extends the existing local command connection with an explicit timed override; it requires an energy site already paired with its Powerwall for local control.

pullRequests.title: Add local Powerwall battery dispatch actions to Teslemetry

articles.title: FIP joins Music Assistant with live song details
articles.dek: Radio France’s music station and twelve themed streams identify what is playing.
body: Music Assistant adds FIP and its twelve themed webradios as music sources. Alongside the audio, the connection shows the current song, artist and artwork, or the programme’s name and picture during live shows.

FIP’s streams carry no song information, so Matthias Cullmann’s connection reads the public services used by Radio France’s own player. It follows the announced next song to compensate for delayed song updates. The thirteen stations support browsing and search.

pullRequests.title: Add FIP provider with live song details for FIP and its webradios
Tell Music Assistant FIP's streams are 48 kHz, so they are not resampled twice

articles.title: Music Assistant lets personal files supply artist biographies and artwork
articles.dek: Local information can cover streaming artists and compilation guests, even with online lookups disabled.
body: Music Assistant reads a personal artist-information folder to supply biographies and artwork, including for artists who have no music folder of their own. That covers supporting artists, compilation appearances and artists heard through streaming services.

The new Local metadata connection reads Kodi-style folders and artist.nfo files. Local descriptions replace online values and still work with online lookups disabled. It only reads the folder; when that folder cannot be reached, existing information stays in place until a later retry.

pullRequests.title: Add a Local metadata provider for a Kodi style artist information folder

articles.title: Home Assistant finds music in a listener’s private accounts
articles.dek: Music Assistant searches receive the same household identity already used for playback.
body: Home Assistant passes the requesting user’s identity into Music Assistant searches. A music source belonging to that person but not shared with everyone could previously return empty search results, even while playback from the same source worked.
The correction lets Music Assistant apply its account permissions to the person making the search. It sends the identity reference only to servers that support this account lookup.

pullRequests.title: Search Music Assistant as the calling user

articles.title: ESPHome stops album artwork from crashing voice satellites
articles.dek: JPEG images use external memory where available and are skipped if memory runs out.
body: ESPHome changes how it loads JPEG images after album artwork caused an ESP32-S3 voice satellite to freeze or restart. The image decoder could reserve nearly 18 kilobytes of internal memory after the audio system had already taken its buffers, leaving too little room to keep the device running.

The decoder uses external RAM first when the board provides it. If there is still not enough memory, the image is skipped with an error instead of aborting the device. Boards without external RAM keep using internal memory but gain the same failure handling.
JoHoenk makes their first contribution to ESPHome with the correction, reviewed by Clyde Stubbs.

pullRequests.title: [runtime_image] Allocate the JPEG decoder state from PSRAM and tolerate a failed allocation

articles.title: Linux Voice Assistant keeps the chosen assistant for follow-up questions
articles.dek: Two wake words can continue using their respective agents and voices.
body: Linux Voice Assistant keeps a continued conversation with the assistant selected by its wake word. With two wake words assigned to different Home Assistant voice pipelines, a conversation begun with the second could switch to the first for its follow-up, changing both the agent and its spoken voice.

ChrisB85 makes a first contribution to Linux Voice Assistant by retaining the original wake phrase when the satellite reopens the microphone. Conversations started by a button or a Home Assistant announcement keep using the first pipeline as before.

pullRequests.title: Keep wake word phrase on continued conversation

articles.title: Sendspin lets another server pair while a player is connected
articles.dek: The command-line player follows connection priority instead of keeping an idle server in control.
body: Sendspin’s command-line player lets a second server pair while Music Assistant already holds a connection to it. Previously, the player rejected the pairing attempt when the first server was idle, preventing people from adding another server without first freeing the player.

The player hands incoming connections to the shared Sendspin client, which chooses between pairing, playback and idle connections. Willem Vooijs tested pairing and playback takeover in both directions using Music Assistant 2.10.8 and a macOS Sendspin 1.0 server.

pullRequests.title: Let aiosendspin arbitrate the daemon's server connections

articles.title: Home Assistant refreshes Google Assistant settings without restarting
articles.dek: Manually configured connections can apply exposure and entity changes through a reload action.
body: Home Assistant adds a reload action for manually configured Google Assistant connections. Changes to exposed domains, individual entities and other YAML settings take effect without restarting the whole Home Assistant system.

The action reads the configuration again, updates the running connection and synchronizes the entities with Google. The ordinary YAML reload previously could not do this because the integration had no reload action.

pullRequests.title: Add reload service to Google Assistant
Document google_assistant.reload action

articles.title: ESPHome stops crash reports from trapping devices in repeated restarts
articles.dek: A saved fault report no longer causes another fault while checking invalid addresses.
body: ESPHome prevents a saved crash report from keeping some RISC-V ESP32 devices in a restart loop. After one fault, printing the report could read an unmapped memory address, crash again and save another report that repeated the same failure at the next boot.

Clyde Stubbs limits those checks to accessible program code. In a deliberately induced fault test on an ESP32-P4 M5Stack Tab5 with external RAM enabled, the old code restarted 25 times in 40 seconds; the correction printed the original report once and booted normally.

pullRequests.title: [esp32] Check that code is mapped before reading it in the crash report

articles.title: Music Assistant pauses more Cast apps without disconnecting them
articles.dek: Controls follow the commands reported by the running app, with a correction for Tidal.
body: Music Assistant gives externally started Cast sessions the controls their apps support. Tidal previously received no controls because its name appeared in uppercase, so a pause was treated as a stop that quit the app and disconnected the casting phone.

The connection also reads the available commands for apps outside its known list, such as TuneIn, after they load media. Those apps can expose their supported pause, seek or queue controls instead of receiving no controls at all.

pullRequests.title: Chromecast: offer a cast app the controls it can take

articles.title: Home Assistant lets AI assistants reload a failing integration
articles.dek: The administrator management connection gains a recovery action alongside its inspection tools.
body: AI assistants using Home Assistant’s system-management connection gain an action to reload an installed integration connection. It can retry a connection after a transient setup failure or apply changes without requiring the person to find the integration’s reload control.

This extends the inspection tools covered on October 24 with a specific recovery action. The management connection requires an administrator and has broader access than the household entities exposed to Assist.

pullRequests.title: Add ReloadConfigEntryTool and short config entry IDs to config LLM tools
Add Home Assistant LLM API and system log tool
Add GetConfigEntriesTool LLM tool to config integration

articles.title: Linux Voice Assistant signals when a request ends without an answer
articles.dek: A short sound distinguishes an ended session from one that is still listening.
body: Linux Voice Assistant plays a sound when a request ends without a spoken reply, such as after a timeout, an error or no detected speech. Previously, it returned silently to idle, leaving people unsure whether it was still listening.

David Markey makes a first contribution to Linux Voice Assistant with the cue, which is enabled by default and can be changed or disabled. It does not play after a spoken reply or while a conversation continues, and paused music resumes after the sound finishes.

pullRequests.title: feat: add pipeline ended sound

articles.title: Home Assistant’s iPhone app signs in again without removing a server
articles.dek: A settings action handles a changed password or switching the account used for that server.
body: Home Assistant’s iPhone app adds a Re-authenticate action in a server’s details and its settings menu. It starts a fresh sign-in without removing the saved server, including after a password change or when switching users.
The app asks which address to use when several are configured and requests a required client certificate if none is stored. The server view reloads after sign-in.

pullRequests.title: Allow re-authenticating a server from settings

articles.title: One unresponsive HEOS device no longer hides every player
articles.dek: Setup skips a failed input lookup and keeps discovering the other devices.
body: Music Assistant keeps discovering HEOS players when one device’s auxiliary inputs cannot be read. Previously, setup browsed every device together, so one timeout could fail the entire connection and leave no HEOS players visible.
The connection checks devices separately and skips a failed lookup, allowing the others to finish setup.

pullRequests.title: Don't fail HEOS setup when one device's inputs can't be browsed
